nodes.description: owner — address of the contract owner, assigned from msg.sender in the Owned constructor and used by the onlyOwner modifier.
newOwner — pending owner address used during the two-step ownership transfer.
symbol — public token symbol string set in the NarcoDoge constructor.
name — public token name string set in the NarcoDoge constructor.
decimals — public uint8 token decimals set to 18.
_totalSupply — total token supply; set in the constructor and read by totalSupply().
balances — mapping(address => uint) holding each account token balance.
allowed — nested mapping(address => mapping(address => uint)) holding spend allowances.
SafeMath.safeAdd(uint a, uint b) — returns a + b with an overflow require check.
SafeMath.safeSub(uint a, uint b) — returns a - b with a underflow require check.
SafeMath.safeMul(uint a, uint b) — returns a * b with an overflow require check.
SafeMath.safeDiv(uint a, uint b) — returns a / b with a division-by-zero require check.
Owned() — constructor that sets owner = msg.sender.
transferOwnership(address _newOwner) — onlyOwner; stages a new owner in newOwner.
acceptOwnership() — requires msg.sender == newOwner, then promotes newOwner to owner.
NarcoDoge() — constructor that sets symbol, name, decimals, total supply and credits the full supply to a fixed address.
totalSupply() — returns _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] using a raw unchecked subtraction.
balanceOf(address tokenOwner) — returns balances[tokenOwner].
transfer(address to, uint tokens) — moves tokens from msg.sender to to using SafeMath.
approve(address spender, uint tokens) — sets allowed[msg.sender][spender] with no double-spend check.
transferFrom(address from, address to, uint tokens) — debits balances and allowance, credits recipient.
allowance(address tokenOwner, address spender) — returns allowed[tokenOwner][spender].
approveAndCall(address spender, uint tokens, bytes data) — sets allowance then calls spender.receiveApproval externally.
fallback() payable — unconditionally reverts, rejecting all plain ETH transfers.
transferAnyERC20Token(address tokenAddress, uint tokens) — onlyOwner; performs an external call on an arbitrary ERC20 contract.
msg.sender — caller-controlled address used for authorization checks and balance/allowance ownership.
tx.origin — transaction origin input available to the contract (not referenced in this code).
Unchecked subtraction _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] inside totalSupply() without SafeMath.
Raw addition c = a + b in safeAdd (guarded by require(c >= a)).
Raw subtraction c = a - b in safeSub (guarded by require(b <= a)).
Raw multiplication c = a * b in safeMul (guarded by require(a == 0 || c / a == b)).
Raw division c = a / b in safeDiv (guarded by require(b > 0)).
External call ApproveAndCallFallBack(spender).receiveApproval(msg.sender, tokens, this, data) executed after allowance state change.
External call ERC20Interface(tokenAddress).transfer(owner, tokens) on a caller-supplied contract address.

msg.sender is the spender whose allowance is decremented in transferFrom.

Owned constructor assigns owner = msg.sender with no validation.
onlyOwner modifier requires msg.sender == owner before transferOwnership body executes.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner to promote ownership.
onlyOwner modifier gates the external call in transferAnyERC20Token.

safeDiv performs the raw division c = a / b.

transferFrom uses safeSub for both balance and allowance debits.
transferFrom uses safeAdd to credit the recipient balance.

transfer mutates the balances mapping.
transferFrom mutates the balances mapping.
transferFrom decrements the allowed allowance mapping.
approveAndCall writes the allowance before performing the external call.
approveAndCall invokes an arbitrary spender contract via receiveApproval after state changes.
The receiveApproval callback can re-enter and manipulate the allowed allowance mapping.
The re-entrant callback can invoke transferFrom and move balances before the caller returns.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external call on a caller-supplied token contract.
The arbitrary external token contract could re-enter owner-gated functions during the call.

acceptOwnership reads and then clears newOwner.
acceptOwnership promotes newOwner into the owner state variable.
